Nothing qualified as a quick win, so I left the queue unchanged. I read all 14 open tickets. None is held by anyone or has a pull request, and the agent queue is empty.

I only counted a ticket as a quick win if its plan showed low effort and no uncertainty. Every plan has an uncertainty of at least 4. The lowest-effort tickets still have real uncertainty:

| Ticket | Effort | Uncertainty |
|---|---|---|
| An Actions agent is told two branch names | 2 | 5 |
| Dashboard UX notes | 2 | 5 |
| Cursor parity checklist | 3 | 8 |
| Follow-ups from the cold reads | 3 | 6 |
| Browser Phase 2 (bundle Chromium into the sandbox image) | 3 | 7 |

The other nine have effort 4 to 8 and uncertainty 4 to 7. The lowest uncertainty is 4, on "Interrupt the current turn", which has effort 5.

To get any of these worked, someone has to settle the open choices in its plan first; the two effort-2 tickets are the cheapest candidates. Then its uncertainty can drop to 0 and a later triage would queue it.
